verdict.rationale: Knowledge provides its own scoped storage: each customer's or team's pages live in their own scope, and the scopes passed for a run decide what it can read. Search only returns pages the run can read, so a run holding a different org scope cannot find Acme's page. Permissions are also documented at individual, team and org level. Per-agent and per-application scoping are not explicitly documented, since the evidence shows multiple agents sharing one scope. Missing for 10: explicit per-agent and per-application scoping, independent or hands-on verification of tenant isolation in retrieval, and isolation guarantees beyond vendor claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scope memories per user, agent, or application so one tenant's memories never leak into another's retrieval
